152 THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

picture of the two paths of life, of those who are satisfied to be 'Hewers of wood and drawers of water' and those who are not. It really was great and inspiring! You ask your teacher if he remembers it. I recall also his habit, when he would roll out at us such a sentence as 'Mirabile dictu' (meaning something interesting), followed by some Latin 'jiberties' that sounded like 'et tu brute moron.' The audience seldom knew what he had said, but the knowledge I have is in my experience. I may find it—I find it in my copy. It always had the desired effect of scaring me speechless.

Among the echoes of this attitude of many an ex-student is one from Mrs. Lena Pann Hodges, of Hollywood, California, gleaned from a fifty-fifth or fifty-sixth wedding anniversary as of last month. It may surprise you for me to mention that I was a very poor speller, and there was a time when my spelling teacher was Miss Lula Chase—now Mrs. Wray—wife of the third judge of the court, I believe. Her address is Mrs. W. H. Wray, of Gaines, or McLennan[?] County, Texas.

Reverend Lewis Holland and J. H. Holland began at Savoy College as early as 1885-1886, and the enrollment enlarged with the name changed to the Western Baptist. Dr. Haskell having acquired an interest in the Baptist, was known as the Western Baptist. In 1905, the institution was known as the Western Baptist and became a paper to the Baptist Standard, and which was known as the Baptist Standard, and was its Secretary to the State dis-trict board, was a delegate of the Baptist Convention, was Vice-President of the Howard College, and was President of the Board of Florence University for many years—a loyal contributor to university at large for many years to 1903 to 1938, being Secretary to the State convention, until Jesus comes again.

${ }^{1}$Personal letter from Mrs. Lena Pace, in The Savoy Star, July 17, 1938, p. 81.
